moved.sentence: Choose names that are unlikely to repeat across levels, and document the shadowing in the install report.

judged.note: Both instructions kept at SHOULD (names unlikely to repeat across levels, shadowing documented in the install report); the merge-levels context stays in the collisions-in-names-that-merge part.

moved.sentence: Print one line per skipped file: the path, why it was skipped, and what the user can do (rename theirs, or install with your own prefix).

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with all three items per line (path, why skipped, what the user can do) and both remedies.

moved.sentence: Exit with a non-zero status when any file was skipped for a conflict, so automation notices.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with its condition (any file skipped for a conflict) and reason (so automation notices).
Kept at SHOULD; the rule also carries the following elaboration on prefixes or own directory and why.
Kept at SHOULD with the full decision procedure for identical, previously installed, and foreign targets.
Kept at SHOULD with both mechanisms (in-file marker or manifest) and the reason (updates and uninstalls touch only your files).

moved.sentence: Never fix a collision by renaming the user's file or by removing it.

judged.note: 'Never' is kept as MUST NOT, along with the alternative (rename or skip your own).

moved.sentence: Uninstall removes only files recorded as yours, and only if they still match what you wrote.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with both conditions (recorded as yours, still matching), plus the handling of user-edited files.

moved.sentence: Do the check in the installer, not in the shipped file.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: the collision check lives in the installer, not the shipped file.

moved.sentence: A skill must not rely on being the only one with its name.

judged.note: The lowercase 'must not' is strengthened to MUST NOT, with the same scope.

moved.sentence: Make installs idempotent: running one twice leaves the same files and reports no conflict with itself.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the full definition of idempotent (same files, no conflict with itself).
